summary:
ASTRA Health is an AI-powered health monitoring app for astronauts on long-duration missions, where doctors are far away and ground contact is delayed. It combines three tools in one platform: a real-time health dashboard, an AI medical assistant, and a predictive health system.

The dashboard tracks heart rate, blood pressure, temperature, sleep and mood. It shows an overall status, flags unusual readings, and displays seven-day trends alongside daily exercise, hydration and check-in reminders. Each astronaut’s data is compared with their own pre-mission baseline rather than general averages, so small changes are caught early. When an alert appears, the astronaut can describe symptoms to the AI assistant. It checks their recent vitals and records, explains likely causes, says when to seek medical help, and suggests sleep, exercise and stress actions. It gives guidance only, not a diagnosis.

The project draws on NASA open science data (OSDR OSD-575, the Inspiration4 blood serum study) covering metabolic, cardiovascular and immune health, along with simulated astronaut records. It addresses the challenge by supporting autonomous, personalised care far from Earth, which makes long missions safer and more sustainable.
details:
ASTRA Health is an AI-powered health companion for astronauts on long missions, far from doctors and with delayed ground contact. A dashboard tracks heart rate, blood pressure, temperature, sleep and mood, shows an overall status with alerts, and gives seven-day trends and daily reminders for exercise, hydration and check-ins. Each astronaut is compared with their own pre-mission baseline, so small changes are caught early.

When an alert appears, they can describe their symptoms to an AI assistant that checks their recent vitals and records, explains likely causes, and says when to seek medical help. Predictive analytics then spot trends and suggest sleep, exercise and stress actions. We built it with Node.js and FastAPI, using TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, HTML, CSS and JSON. The assistant has an offline rule-based mode that works with no network, plus an optional online mode powered by the Groq API.

The project is grounded in NASA open science data (OSDR OSD-575, the Inspiration4 blood serum study) covering metabolic, cardiovascular and immune health, combined with simulated astronaut records. It is creative because it replaces generic averages with a personal baseline and brings monitoring, AI guidance and prediction together in one app that still works offline. We considered safety (the AI gives guidance only, not a diagnosis), limited connectivity, data privacy and the effects of microgravity on the body.
